arxiv-2105-00424.title: In-cell Discontinuous Reconstruction path-conservative methods for non conservative hyperbolic systems - Second-order extension Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2105-00424.creator: Ernesto Pimentel-García, Manuel J. Castro, Christophe Chalons, Tomás Morales de Luna, Carlos Parés
arxiv-2105-00424.description: Abstract We are interested in the numerical approximation of discontinuous solutions in non conservative hyperbolic systems. An extension to second-order of a new strategy based on in-cell discontinuous reconstructions to deal with this challenging topic is presented. This extension is based on the combination of the first-order in-cell reconstruction and the MUSCL-Hancock reconstruction.

arxiv-2212-00126.title: Proton Computed Tomography Based on Richardson – Lucy Algorithm Journal: Phys. Med. Biol.
arxiv-2212-00126.creator: Gábor Bíró, Ákos Sudár, Zsófia Jólesz, Gábor Papp, Gergely Gábor Barnaföldi for the Bergen pCT collaboration
arxiv-2212-00126.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gábor Bíró, Ákos Sudár, Zsófia Jólesz, Gábor Papp, Gergely Gábor Barnaföldi for the Bergen pCT collaboration. Objective: Proton therapy is an emerging method in cancer therapy. One of the main developments is to increase the accuracy of the Bragg-peak position calculation, which requires more precise relative stopping power (RSP) measurements. An excellent choice is the application of proton computed tomography (pCT) systems which takes the images under similar conditions, as they use the same irradiation device and hadron beam for imaging and treatment.

arxiv-2309-12119.title: Pseudo-Bayesian unit level modeling for small area estimation under informative sampling
arxiv-2309-12119.creator: Peter A. Gao, Jon Wakefield
arxiv-2309-12119.description: Abstract When mapping subnational health and demographic indicators, direct weighted estimators of small area means based on household survey data can be unreliable when data are limited. If survey microdata are available, unit level models can relate individual survey responses to unit level auxiliary covariates and explicitly account for spatial dependence and between area variation using random effects.

arxiv-2401-07378.creator: Guangyu Meng, Ruyu Zhou, Liu Liu, Peixian Liang, Fang Liu, Danny Z. Chen, Michael Niemier, Xiaobo Sharon Hu Department of Computer Science, Engineering, University of Notre Dame, USA
arxiv-2401-07378.description: Abstract Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) is an important similarity measure between two distributions, commonly used in computer vision and many other application domains. However, its exact calculation is computationally and memory intensive, which hinders its scalability and applicability for large-scale problems.

arxiv-2509-01481.title: Ideal Optical Flux Lattices
arxiv-2509-01481.creator: Ophelia Evelyn Sommer, Nigel R. Cooper
arxiv-2509-01481.description: Abstract The realization of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states in cold atomic gases is a long-standing goal in quantum simulation. Established approaches, including rapidly rotating gases and tight-binding lattices, are often hampered by low interaction energies and small many-body energy gaps.

arxiv-2510-05371.title: Zigzags and free adjunctions
arxiv-2510-05371.creator: Lorenzo Riva, Martina Rovelli
arxiv-2510-05371.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Riva, Martina Rovelli. We construct an explicit combinatorial model of the functor which adds right adjoints to the morphisms of an ∞ \infty -category, and we speculate on possible extensions to higher dimensions. Motivation: adding adjoints Fix an (\infty,n) -category \mathscr{C} and two k -morphisms f:x\to y and g:y\to x in \mathscr{C} between parallel (k-1) -morphisms x and y .

arxiv-2602-07681.title: Mapping Drivers of Greenness: Spatial Variable Selection for MODIS Vegetation Indices
arxiv-2602-07681.creator: Qishi Zhan, Cheng-Han Yu, Yuchi Chen, Zhikang Dong, Rajarshi Guhaniyogi
arxiv-2602-07681.description: Abstract Understanding how environmental drivers relate to vegetation condition motivates spatially varying regression models, but estimating a separate coefficient surface for every predictor can yield noisy patterns and poor interpretability when many predictors are irrelevant. Motivated by MODIS vegetation index studies, we examine predictors from spectral bands, productivity and energy fluxes, observation geometry, and land surface characteristics.

pmc-10557104.title: Challenges and successful management of subglottic tracheal stenosis in a 2‑year‑old child: A case report and a mini‑review of the literature
pmc-10557104.creator: Fahmi H. Kakamad, Mariwan L. Fatah, Rezheen J. Rashid, Karzan M. Hasan, Bilal A. Mohammed, Honar Othman Kareem, Sarwat T. San Ahmed, Khdir Hussein Hamad Khoshnaw, Sanaa O. Karim, Berun A. Abdalla, Sarhang Sedeeq Abdullah
pmc-10557104.description: Tracheal stenosis is a narrowing of the windpipe that can lead to shortness of breath, stridor and even suffocation. The present study reports the clinical course of a patient with this condition in an aim to help clinicians obtain more information about this rare condition and identify potential treatment options.

pmc-10605511.title: Association of nutritional status and comorbidity with long-term survival among community-dwelling older males
pmc-10605511.creator: Baicun Hou, Yunjuan Lin, Wangjingyi Zhang, Qiqi Lin, Shengshu Wang, Fansen Meng, Wei Dai, Gangshi Wang
pmc-10605511.description: BackgroundEstimates of survival in the older can be of benefit in various facets, particularly in medical and individual decision-making. We aim to validate the value of a combination of nutrition status evaluation and comorbidity assessment in predicting long-term survival among community-dwelling older.MethodsThe Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was applied for comprehensive evaluation of comorbidities.

pmc-12492775.title: Joint effects of triglyceride glucose index and its obesity-related derivatives with estimated glucose disposal rate on cardiometabolic multimorbidity in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: a nationwide cohort study
pmc-12492775.creator: Xianlin Ruan, Yihang Ling, Jinming Chen, Yulong Xiang, Huangtao Ruan, Weipeng Zhang, Ling Jing, Xin Gao, Yibo He, Xiaozhao Lu, Tian Chang, Junyan Xu, Jiyan Chen
pmc-12492775.description: BackgroundThe triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) serve as surrogate markers of insulin resistance (IR) and are associated with cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs). However, the joint effects of TyG-related indices and eGDR on cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) risk remains unclear.

pmc-12504159.title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCH9 alleviates pyroptosis by regulating NLPR3 ubiquitination following myocardial ischemia reperfusion
pmc-12504159.creator: Hongquan Lu, Gang Ma, Cong Ding, Ping Wang, Qiuyue Ruan, Yun Zeng, Lingkun Ma, Min Lu, Yilin Li, Wenjing Sun
pmc-12504159.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). NLRP3, a member of the NOD-like receptor family, mediates pyroptosis via inflammasome activation, contributing significantly to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (MI/R) injury. However, the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying NLRP3 inflammasome activation and its role in pyroptotic myocyte death following MI/R injury, with a particular focus on the effects of MARCH9, an E3 ubiquitin ligase that encodes a RING finger domain.

pmc-12588528.title: Impact of agricultural subsidy on chemical fertilizer use: Empirical evidence of China’s Organic-Substitute-Chemical-Fertilizer policy based on double machine learning
pmc-12588528.creator: Lei Deng, Pengcheng Wan, Fangyu Ye, Jingjie Zhao
pmc-12588528.description: The sustainable development of agriculture hinges on effective fertilizer management, and China’s experience with chemical fertilizer overuse highlights the challenges and opportunities in this domain. This study examines the impact of agricultural subsidy policy on chemical fertilizer use across 2319 counties from 2012 to 2022.

pmc-12656889.title: Underreporting of Adverse Events Following COVID-19 Vaccination Among Healthcare Professionals in Poland: Potential Implications for Vaccine Hesitancy
pmc-12656889.creator: Jakub Grabowski, Anna Niebrzydowska, Aleksandra Brzozowska, Przemysław Waszak, Paweł Zagożdżon, Shan Ali, Tomasz Brancewicz, Monika Wolff, Aleksandra Macul-Sanewska, Leszek Bidzan
pmc-12656889.description: This study aimed to assess the prevalence and reporting rate of adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) among healthcare professionals (HCPs) and students of health-related disciplines after COVID-19 vaccination. It was conducted at the beginning of the vaccination campaign in Poland (February 2021), when vaccines were only available to limited groups of recipients, mainly those related to healthcare.

pmc-13387632.creator: Mary L Ohmer, Leah A Jacobs, Jason Beery, Anthony Fabio, Kim Falk, Ivana Gazarik, Christi Gomez, Tracey Joiner, Elizabeth Miller, Alex Neumann, Aaleah Oliver, Ross Reilly, Mohammad R Shedeed, April Zeiner, Alison J Culyba, Javad Sarvestan
pmc-13387632.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCommunity and youth violence are pervasive and have devastating health, economic, and social consequences. Violence too often impacts people of color and the life trajectories of youth in the United States, especially among people living in urban settings.ObjectiveIn response, this study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a novel Community Resiliency Collective Efficacy Intervention (CRCEI), which seeks to increase individual and neighborhood levels of collective efficacy, and reduce youth and community violence.

uslaw-usc-t18-s475.title: 18 U.S.C. § 475 — Imitating obligations or securities; advertisements
uslaw-usc-t18-s475.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s475.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 25 (Counterfeiting And Forgery). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever designs, engraves, prints, makes, or executes, or utters, issues, distributes, circulates, or uses any business or professional card, notice, placard, circular, handbill, or advertisement in the likeness or similitude of any obligation or security of the United States issued.
